# Yinshi Cross-Cutting Architecture Report

Scope is `backend/src/yinshi` (Python, FastAPI), `frontend/src` (React, Vite), `desktop/src` (Electron, TypeScript), and `sidecar/src` (Node). Vendored and build directories were excluded.

## 1. Noise IK and encryption protocol

There is no single authoritative definition. No shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact exist. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript. Matching literal constants are written twice.

The handshake layer duplicates every constant across the language boundary.

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue and protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23`, `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two sides use different crypto stacks. Python uses `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` at `runner_noise.py:11-20`. The browser uses `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` at `noiseIk.ts:1-6`. Parity is maintained only by hand.

Capability tokens are issued and verified only in Python, at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306`. The Ed25519-signed claims are `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, and `protocol`. The runner responder consumes them at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225`. It sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend re-validates the same claim shape independently. See the `RunnerCapabilityResponse` interface at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` and `validateCapability` at `:118`. The handshake reply is parsed at `:449-452`.

The relay framing layer adds a 16-byte UUID prefix that only the Python endpoints understand. The hosted relay adds the prefix on client-to-runner traffic at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283`, as `uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`. It strips the prefix on runner-to-client traffic at `:298-330`. The runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`. Control messages are hand-built JSON strings rather than models. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`. Those strings are parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`. The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

The RPC envelope layer carries a version mismatch. The frontend request envelope sends `v: 2` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484`. The backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17` and lacks `query`. Version and type checks run at `:83-100`. The response envelope is built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325`. It is parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500`. Size limits diverge by construction. The browser caps a request at 49152 bytes at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`. The responder caps the frame from the capability at `runner_noise_session.py:265-271`. The relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` at `runner_relay.py:271`. The version-name mismatch and the missing `query` key are both open risks.

Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme. `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}` and passes those values to the Python helper. The backend reads them through settings. It derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers at `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` only detects FileVault status through `detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`. It takes no part in the Noise protocol.

A protocol change requires coordinated edits in seventeen places. On the backend, `services/runner_noise.py` holds handshake primitives and length bounds. `services/runner_noise_session.py` holds the prologue, capability binding, handshake reply, and frame limits. `services/runner_capabilities.py` holds the protocol tag, claim schema, and scope set. `services/runner_rpc.py` holds the envelope, version, and route-to-scope table. `services/runner_relay.py` holds prefix framing, control JSON, and byte limits. `services/runner_agent_relay.py` holds runner-side demux. `api/runner_relay.py` holds the WebSocket endpoints. `api/runners.py` holds capability issuance, with the protocol echoed at `:198`. `runner_agent.py` holds the relay client, registration, and key pinning. `models.py` holds `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn:370`, `RunnerCapabilityOut:393`, `RunnerRegisterIn:324`, and `RunnerNoiseKeyConfirmationIn:360`. On the frontend the affected files are `crypto/noiseIk.ts`, `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts`, `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts`, `runtime/encryptedUpload.ts`, `runner/repositories.ts`, and `types/noise-c-wasm.d.ts`. Inside `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` the relevant points are scope selection and the session byte budget at `:92`. Test mirrors also change. Those are `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.test.ts`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.test.ts`, and the backend suites for the five services above. Desktop is affected only when the `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts` route allowlist must change. Section 3 covers that case.

## 2. Type and schema duplication

There is no OpenAPI codegen. `frontend/package.json` has no `openapi` or generate script. The backend serves `/openapi.json` only when `debug` is true, at `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:451`. Every API shape is hand-written twice. Pydantic models live in `backend/src/yinshi/models.py`. TypeScript interfaces live in `frontend/src/api/client.ts`.

| Shape | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo | `models.py:136` `RepoOut` | `client.ts:1` `Repo` |
| Workspace | `models.py:163` `WorkspaceOut` | `client.ts:178` `Workspace` |
| Session | `models.py:212` `SessionOut` | `client.ts:189` `SessionInfo` |
| Message | `models.py:224` `MessageOut` | `client.ts:199` `Message` |
| CloudRunner | `models.py:294` `CloudRunnerOut` | `client.ts:83` `CloudRunner` |
| Runner registration | `models.py:314` `CloudRunnerRegistrationOut` | `client.ts:101` `CloudRunnerRegistration` |
| Runner capability response | `models.py:393` `RunnerCapabilityOut` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14` `RunnerCapabilityResponse` |
| Runner capability request | `models.py:370` `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:27` `RunnerCapabilityRequest` |
| Provider descriptor | `models.py:448` | `client.ts:34` |
| Provider setup field | `models.py:439` | `client.ts:27` |
| Model descriptor | `models.py:460` | `client.ts:47` |
| Provider catalog | `models.py:475` | `client.ts:60` |
| Provider auth start | `models.py:483` | `client.ts:109` |
| Provider auth status | `models.py:495` | `client.ts:119` |
| Provider connection | `models.py:602` | `client.ts:66` |
| API key | `models.py:625` | `client.ts:19` |
| Pi config | `models.py:672` | `client.ts:131` |
| Pi command | `models.py:687` | `client.ts:146` |
| Pi config commands | `models.py:702` | `client.ts:153` |
| Pi package release | `models.py:713` | `client.ts:157` |
| Pi release notes | `models.py:724` | `client.ts:166` |
| Prompt request | `models.py:237` `WSPrompt` | inline at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:42-49` and `client.ts:514-522` |

More duplications sit outside `models.py`. Terminal channel shapes appear at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:36-61`. They appear again as hand validators at `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:11-59`, with the event-type set at `:4-9`. Prompt run shapes appear at `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` and at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-40`. The run status enum is duplicated at `promptStream.ts:9-28`. The SSE event union at `frontend/src/api/client.ts:453-502` mirrors sidecar content shaping at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:244-250`. The desktop IPC contract in `desktop/src/desktopApi.ts` is duplicated for the renderer in `frontend/src/types/desktop.d.ts`. The runtime secrets contract at `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` is mirrored by backend settings used in `backend/src/yinshi/config.py` and `services/crypto.py`.

## 3. Runtime abstraction and where the runtime decision is made

This is the key finding. Two orthogonal runtime axes exist, and they are not unified.

Axis A is the frontend `RuntimeRef.location`, with values `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`. It is defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`. The unresolved variant sits at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`. Axis B is the backend `AppMode`, with values `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`. It is selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` through `create_app(mode=...)`. The names do not line up. Frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop`. Frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` inside `runner_agent`. Frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted`. Nothing in the code states or enforces that mapping.

The frontend branches on runtime in thirteen places. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` is the canonical resolution. It parses the encoded ID, resolves the ref, and builds the transport. In `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts`, `defaultRuntimeRef` at `:62-67` returns `local` on desktop and `hosted` elsewhere. `runtimeResourceId` at `:69-83` encodes the runtime into the URL as `hosted.`, `local.`, or `byoc.<b64url>.`. `parseRuntimeResourceId` at `:87-119` decodes it. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner` and requiring `noise_key_confirmed`. Three branches sit in `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts`. Lines `259-273` select `hostedApi` against `api` when the location is hosted and `window.yinshiDesktop` exists. Lines `286-296` dispatch BYOC requests through the encrypted Noise channel. Lines `322-340` branch uploads across BYOC encryption, the hosted bridge, and plain multipart. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` sets the poll delay by runtime location. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` routes to the bridge using the hard-coded `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` set. That route bypasses `RuntimeRef` entirely. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` namespaces the cache key by runtime. `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:172-247, 269, 514, 973, 1096, 1132, 1161` discovers and aggregates all three locations. It rebuilds the default runtime at `:172-174` instead of calling `defaultRuntimeRef`. `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:604-606, 631-638, 697, 716, 757-764` holds a third open-coded copy of that rule at `:604-606` and `:697`.

The backend branches on mode in twelve places. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-424` validates the mode inside `create_app`. Worker mode uses a distinct middleware stack and returns early at `:309-322`. Desktop mode injects `DesktopTenantMiddleware` with the fixed `desktop-local` tenant at `:344-352`. Desktop mode also uses a different content security policy at `:361-363`. `_include_routes` at `:379-412` splits execution routers from control routers. Only hosted mode receives auth, runners, the relay, GitHub, and desktop devices. Hosted-only startup work runs at `:266`. The runner agent builds `create_app(mode="worker", ...)` in-process at `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264-293`. `WorkerHttpDispatcher` at `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-40` asserts `app.state.mode == "worker"` and dispatches over ASGI with no socket. An execution-time branch sits at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:97-105`. With no sidecar socket path it uses the settings socket and the host workspace path. Otherwise it remaps the path into the container. The mechanism behind that branch is `TenantSidecarContext` with a nullable `socket_path` at `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar_runtime.py:30-38`. A separate desktop terminal WebSocket proxy runs at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:188-274`, parallel to the polling channel API. The route-to-scope table at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` gates what a BYOC runtime may execute.

Desktop branches in four places. `desktop/src/main.ts:369` and `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:120-160` set helper and sidecar socket paths and environment. `desktop/src/localRuntime.ts:15-30` asserts that helper and sidecar agree on `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH` before starting the pair. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` allowlists hosted API routes reachable through the bridge. That is the third copy of the route table. `desktop/src/helperSupervisor.ts` and `desktop/src/sidecarSupervisor.ts`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:32,48`, own process lifecycle.

The sidecar branches in three places, none about runtime kind. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:937` reads the socket path from `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`. Line `946` toggles dotenv on `SIDECAR_LOAD_DOTENV === "1"`, and desktop sets `"0"` at `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:158`. Lines `1154-1210` hold one message-type dispatch table. The sidecar is runtime-agnostic.

The same URL surface is enumerated three times, in three languages, for three purposes. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` performs authoritative server-side scope enforcement. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` performs client-side scope selection for capability requests. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` performs Electron bridge allowlisting. Any new API route requires edits in all three files plus the FastAPI router. Divergence here is a security-relevant defect class.

## 4. Terminal and agent-stream data paths

The polling terminal channel is required for BYOC and crosses twelve hops. `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:82` posts to `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminals` and polls `/events/{sequence}`, validating events at `:4-9,47-59`. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` wraps each BYOC call in a Noise RPC. `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-520` performs the handshake and encrypted request. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-330` relay UUID-prefixed frames. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116` demuxes to the per-transfer session. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:71-325` parses the envelope, checks scope, and builds the response. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29` dispatches into the worker app over ASGI. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` holds the terminal routes, and `:79-110` resolves workspace paths and the sidecar socket. `backend/src/yinshi/services/terminal_journal.py:85-512` writes newline-delimited JSON to the sidecar socket. It buffers output into sequenced batches at `_append_event:404`, `_split_terminal_data:439`, and `_decode_message:512`. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1184-1210` dispatches the terminal message types. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:982-1082` spawns the pty. `onData` emits `terminal_data` at `:999-1003`, `onExit` emits `terminal_exit` at `:1005-1012`, and ready emits `terminal_ready` at `:1036-1042`.

A second terminal path exists as a direct WebSocket proxy. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:273-274` exposes `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminal`. It carries its own sidecar framing helpers at `_send_sidecar:72`, `_read_sidecar:81`, `_proxy_browser_to_sidecar:92`, `_proxy_sidecar_to_browser:169`, and `_run_desktop_terminal_proxy:188`. Workspace resolution runs at `backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_terminal.py:37`. Sidecar newline-JSON framing therefore exists twice inside the backend, at `terminals.py:72-91` and `terminal_journal.py:478-512`. Terminal event validation exists in Python at `terminal_journal.py:404-454` and again in TypeScript at `terminalChannel.ts:47-59`. The size bounds of 2 to 500 appear at `terminal_channels.py:37-38,49-51` and `terminalChannel.ts:38-45`.

The agent stream also has two paths. The SSE path starts at `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:127-133`, which calls `streamPrompt`. That function posts to `/api/sessions/{id}/prompt` at `frontend/src/api/client.ts:514-570`. Manual SSE line splitting runs at `:551-566`, and `normalizeEvent` runs at `:503-512`. The backend handles `prompt_session` at `backend/src/yinshi/api/stream.py:771-773`, with execution context resolved at `:630`. `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py:39-136` provides newline-JSON transport with an 8 MiB message limit. The sidecar dispatches `query`, `resolve`, and `cancel` at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1203-1209`, shaping content blocks at `:244-250`.

The polled run journal path starts at `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:114-126`, which calls `startRuntimePrompt`. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-249` posts `/runs`, polls `/runs/{id}/events/{seq}`, and posts `/cancel`. It reuses `normalizeEvent` from `client.ts`. `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` holds the routes. `backend/src/yinshi/services/prompt_journal.py:89-515` owns run lifecycle and sequenced batches. `_default_prompt_executor:58` bridges to the same sidecar execution as the SSE path, and remaining hops match. Across the two stream paths, event normalization is shared. Transport, status enums, cancellation, and terminal-status handling are written twice. Compare `client.ts:514-575` with `promptStream.ts:9-249`. Two journals with near-identical sequenced-batch semantics also exist, in `prompt_journal.py` and `terminal_journal.py`.

## 5. Component dependency map

In the frontend, `App.tsx` depends on the pages and `components/Sidebar`. `pages/Session.tsx:19,67` depends on `runtime/useRuntimeResource`. That module depends on `runtime/runtimeRef`, `runtime/resolveRuntime`, and `runtime/runtimeTransport`. `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` depends on `api/client`, `runner/encryptedRunnerClient`, and `runtime/encryptedUpload`. `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` depends on `crypto/noiseIk`, which loads noise-c.wasm. It also depends on `api/client` for capability issuance. `hooks/useAgentStream.ts` depends on both `api/client.streamPrompt` and `runtime/promptStream`. `components/Sidebar.tsx` depends on the runtime modules, `runner/repositories`, and `api/client`. `api/client.ts` depends on `window.yinshiDesktop`, typed in `types/desktop.d.ts`.

In desktop, `main.ts` depends on sixteen local modules, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:21-48`. They cover app control, supervision, launch configuration, secrets, credentials, and disk status. They also cover the hosted gateway, hosted sessions, hosted auth, security, and shell policy. The rest are the auth callback listener, local repository import, automatic updates, and the IPC contract. `preload.ts` depends on `desktopApi` channel names and exposes `window.yinshiDesktop` at `desktop/src/preload.ts:11-30`. `helperSupervisor` spawns the backend in desktop mode through `backend/src/yinshi/desktop_runtime.py`. `sidecarSupervisor` spawns `sidecar/src/index.js` over `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`.

In the backend, `main.py` depends on the `api` routers, middleware, `config`, and `db`. `api/stream.py` and `api/prompt_runs.py` depend on `services/prompt_journal`, which depends on `services/sidecar`. `api/terminal_channels.py` depends on `services/terminal_journal`, `services/workspace_runtime_paths`, `services/sidecar_runtime`, and `services/container`. `api/terminals.py` depends on `services/desktop_terminal` and talks to the sidecar socket directly. `api/runners.py` depends on `services/runners`, `services/runner_capabilities`, and `services/runner_relay`. `runner_agent.py` depends on `services/runner_agent_relay`. That module depends on `services/runner_rpc`, `services/runner_noise_session`, and `services/runner_noise`. `runner_agent.py` also depends on `runner_worker.py`, which imports `main.create_app` and `worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher`. `services/control_encryption` depends on `services/crypto`. In the sidecar, `index.js` depends on `sidecar.js`. That file depends on `git_auth.js`, `git_askpass_client.js`, and `constants.js`, with no dependency on any other component.

Eight couplings deserve attention. An import cycle is broken only by a deferred import. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264` imports `create_app` from `yinshi.main` inside a method body, while `main.py` reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. The backend also imports itself across a network boundary. The BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI app in-process at `runner_worker.py:288`. It calls that app over ASGI with no listening socket, in `worker_runtime.py`. One codebase acts as both control plane and remote worker, separated only by `app.state.mode`. Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages, as described in section 3. That is the highest-risk coupling in the repository. Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist with their own framing. `api/terminals.py` and `api/terminal_channels.py` both talk to the same sidecar through separately written newline-JSON helpers. `api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction. `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` at `client.ts:321-325` hard-codes three paths that must use the Electron bridge. A fourth control-plane path added later would silently take the wrong transport. The default-runtime rule is written three times, at `runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, and `Settings.tsx:604-606` plus `:697`. Terminology drifts across layers. The frontend says `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`. The backend says `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`. Deployment material says runner, sidecar, and helper, and no file records the mapping. The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component. It knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise, and is a clean extraction boundary.

## Start here

Open `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` first. Lines 10-17 define the `RuntimeRef` union that drives every frontend branch. Lines 46-206 hold the route-to-scope table. That table is duplicated in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` and `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170`. Lines 259-340 contain the dispatch that selects plain HTTP, the Electron bridge, or the Noise channel. Read `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` next for the backend mode split.

## Open questions

Is the RPC envelope `v: 2` at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483` intentional against `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `runner_rpc.py:17`? Does the backend accept the `query` key that the frontend always sends, given its absence from `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`? Is `api/terminals.py` still live, or superseded by `api/terminal_channels.py`, since both are registered at `main.py:395-396`? Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` still live, or superseded by `promptStream.ts`, since `useAgentStream.ts:127` still falls back to it?

arguments.content:
# Software Design Review

Date: 2026-08-07
Scope: entire codebase, four components, roughly 40,000 source lines.
Lens: "A Philosophy of Software Design" red-flag checklist.
Status: findings only. Nothing was implemented.

| Component | Path | Non-test lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backend | `backend/src/yinshi/` | 23,124 |
| Frontend | `frontend/src/` | 11,053 |
| Desktop | `desktop/src/` | 3,168 |
| Sidecar | `sidecar/src/` | 2,584 |

Excluded: `backend/.venv`, `node_modules`, `frontend/dist`, `desktop/dist`, `desktop/release`.

---

## Executive summary

The codebase has strong low-level design. Cryptographic primitives, the Noise
handshake, the secure JSON store, and the account lease verifier are deep
modules with simple interfaces. Test coverage is broad, at 55 backend test files
and 20 frontend test files.

The weakness is at the boundaries. The same design decision is written in
several places, and in several cases the copies have already drifted apart.
Three problems recur across every component:

1. One decision has many homes. The API route surface is enumerated four times,
   in three languages. The database schema is written twice. The runner storage
   profile table is written twice. The default-runtime rule is written three
   times.
2. Concepts are split by operation order rather than by information hiding. The
   desktop account is split across two modules by *when* it is used. The backend
   database layer is split across two modules by *which* database it opens.
3. Transport-layer files hold business logic. `api/stream.py` has 770 lines
   before its first route. `Sidebar.tsx` holds six unrelated responsibilities.
   `sidecar.js` holds thirteen.

Two findings are live defects rather than design debt. Both are small to fix.
They are B1 (session map never evicts) and B2 (concurrent token refresh can
revoke the user device).

---

## Part 1: live defects

### B1. The sidecar session map has no removal path

Severity: high. Effort: small.

`sidecar/src/sidecar.js:934` creates `activeSessions`. It is written at `:1655`
and `:1739`, and read at `:1624`, `:1683`, and `:1966`. The only removal is
`clear()` at `:2005`, inside `cleanup()`, which runs at process exit.

There is no delete, no time-to-live, and no size cap. The protocol has no
dispose message, and `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py` never sends one.
Socket close detaches terminals at `:1129-1132` but leaves sessions untouched.

Each retained entry holds a live pi session with model context, a settings
manager, and an open session file handle. See `SessionManager.open` at `:205`.
In the desktop app the sidecar runs for the whole application lifetime, so every
session a user opens stays resident until quit.

The inconsistency inside the same file is instructive. OAuth flows have a
30-minute time-to-live and a cap of 8, at `:35` and `:1368`. Terminals are
removed on exit at `:1017-1020`. Only pi sessions have neither policy.

Suggested fix. Move the map into `pi/sessionRegistry.js` with a maximum entry
count and an idle time-to-live. On eviction, call `unsubscribe()` and
`piSession.dispose()`. Add a `session_release` message so the backend can
release deterministically.

### B2. Two refresh paths race, and the loser revokes the device

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

The backend treats a replayed refresh token as a compromise signal. At
`backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_auth.py:244-255`, presenting an
already-rotated token revokes the whole device and calls
`signal_desktop_device_revoked`.

The desktop app has two independent paths that spend the stored refresh token,
and only one of them is serialised.

- `HostedAccessSession.getAccessToken` at
  `desktop/src/hostedAccessSession.ts:57-84` de-duplicates concurrent refreshes
  through a `#refresh` promise and guards stale writes through `#epoch`. This
  path is correct.
- `DesktopAppController.switchProfile` at `desktop/src/appController.ts:110-121`
  calls `resumeAccount`, which is wired at `desktop/src/main.ts:301-309` to call
  `resumeDesktopAccount` directly. This path never touches `#refresh`.

Both eventually reach `desktop/src/accountSession.ts:88-99`, which posts the
stored refresh token.

The two are wired 25 lines apart in the same function.
`desktop/src/main.ts:285-292` builds `HostedAccessSession` with a callback into
`resumeDesktopAccount`. Then `main.ts:301-309` builds a second closure calling
the same function and pushing the result back in. The same operation appears
twice, in two directions.

A renderer request that triggers a refresh through
`hostedApiGateway` can overlap a profile switch. The second refresh presents a
token the first has already rotated. The backend then revokes the device, and
the user is signed out with no explanation.

Suggested fix is in Part 3, finding D1.

---

## Part 2: one decision, many homes

This is the dominant structural problem. Each item below is information leakage
in the strict sense: a single design decision that a reader must find in several
files, kept consistent only by hand.

### L1. The API route surface is enumerated four times, in three languages

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

| Location | Purpose | Patterns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/src/yinshi/api/*.py` | the actual FastAPI routers | 81 routes |
| `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` | server-side scope enforcement | 21 |
| `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` | client-side scope selection | 18 |
| `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:12-192` | Electron bridge allowlist | 20 |

Adding one route now requires four coordinated edits across three languages.
Nothing enforces the correspondence, and no test asserts that the tables agree.

The copies have already drifted. The backend handles four pi-upload path
patterns at `runner_rpc.py:206-215`. The frontend table has no upload entries at
all, so `runtimeTransport.ts` would reject them. The upload flow works only
because it bypasses the transport layer entirely. See finding F3.

Each table has a defensible reason to exist. The backend table is authoritative
enforcement. The desktop table limits what a compromised renderer can reach. So
deletion is the wrong fix.

Suggested fix. Declare the route-to-scope mapping once, as FastAPI dependency
metadata attached to each route. Build the backend table at startup by walking
the registered routes, so an unregistered route fails loudly instead of becoming
silently unreachable. Generate the frontend and desktop tables at build time from
the OpenAPI document. Divergence then becomes a build failure rather than a
runtime rejection.

### L2. The database schema is written twice, and the migrations have drifted

Severity: high. Effort: large.

`backend/src/yinshi/db.py:33-120` holds `SCHEMA_SQL`. `tenant.py:66-152` holds
`USER_SCHEMA_SQL`. A direct diff of the two regions reports exactly one
difference: `tenant.py` omits the `owner_email` column.

Eighty-seven of eighty-eight lines are duplicated verbatim. That covers six
create-table statements, six indexes, and three triggers. Every column addition
must be made twice.

The migration logic is duplicated too, and it has already produced inconsistent
state. `db.py:342-384` applies five numbered migrations behind a `schema_version`
table. `tenant.py:153-175` applies four of the same column additions with no
version tracking, re-running `PRAGMA table_info` on every call. Both migrations
add `pi_context_version` with a default of zero, at `db.py:379` and
`tenant.py:172-174`. Both base schemas declare a default of one, at `db.py:66`
and `tenant.py:97`. New databases and migrated databases therefore start in
different states.

That inconsistency is not hypothetical. `api/stream.py:571-595` exists to detect
and repair it at request time.

Six SQLCipher helpers are near-duplicates as well.

| Concern | `db.py` | `tenant.py` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Driver module names | 25 | 29-32 |
| Driver loading | 130-140 | 183-204 |
| Keyed connection open | 164-191 | 216-247 |
| Plaintext readability probe | 193-206 | 257-270 |
| Encrypted integrity validation | 208-228 | 299-313 |
| Plaintext to encrypted migration | 230-293 | 315-343 |

The two probes at `tenant.py:257-270` and `db.py:193-206` differ only by one
file-existence call.

Suggested fix. Create `db/schema.py` with one parameterised schema builder and
one ordered migration list keyed by version, applied to both database kinds.
Create `db/sqlcipher.py` holding the driver loader, keyed open, plaintext probe,
integrity validator, and migration, parameterised by a key-derivation callable.
The two current modules then hold only policy and connection scoping. Expect
well under the current combined 1,305 lines.

### L3. The runner storage profile table is duplicated verbatim

Severity: high. Effort: small.

`runner_agent.py:57-121` and `services/runners.py:58-120` hold the same
`RunnerStorageProfileSpec` dataclass with 11 fields, and the same 63-line
`_STORAGE_PROFILES` dictionary with three entries. A direct diff reports only a
one-line docstring difference and a blank line. Every profile value is identical.

The eight supporting constants are duplicated at `runner_agent.py:48-55` and
`services/runners.py:40-47`. So is the storage-profile literal type, at
`runner_agent.py:33-37` and `services/runners.py:24-28`. So is
`_storage_profile_spec`, at `runner_agent.py:182` and `services/runners.py:157`.

The control plane validates reported runner capabilities against this table at
`services/runners.py:313`. The agent uses the same table to choose its own
defaults at `runner_agent.py:212-216`. Editing one copy alone makes runners fail
validation against the control plane, with no local signal.

Suggested fix. Move the literal type, constants, dataclass, dictionary, and
lookup helper into `runner_storage_profiles.py`. Import from both sides. This
deletes about 130 duplicated lines and is the cheapest high-value change in the
report.

### L4. The Noise wire protocol is re-derived independently per language

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

There is no shared schema, IDL, or generated artifact. Matching literal
constants are written twice, in two different crypto stacks. Python uses
`noiseprotocol` at `services/runner_noise.py:11-20`. The browser uses
`@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` at `crypto/noiseIk.ts:1-6`. Parity is maintained
only by hand.

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name | `runner_noise.py:22` | `noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `runner_noise.py:26` | `noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `runner_noise.py:24` | `noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `runner_noise.py:25` | `noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `runner_noise_session.py:24` | `noiseIk.ts:14` |
| Prologue tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `runner_noise_session.py:23` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9` |

A protocol change requires coordinated edits in seventeen files across backend
and frontend, plus their test mirrors.

Two open discrepancies were found while tracing this. The frontend request
envelope sends `v: 2` at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483`, while the backend
accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `runner_rpc.py:17` and does not
list the `query` key the frontend always sends. Both deserve confirmation as
intentional or otherwise. Separately, the session byte cap has three values:
64 KiB at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:15`, 256 KiB at `runtimeTransport.ts:90`,
and 128 MiB at `encryptedUpload.ts:10`.

Suggested fix. Declare the constants and envelope schema in one machine-readable
file. Generate the Python and TypeScript constant modules from it. This will not
unify the two crypto implementations, and it should not try to. It removes the
class of failure where the two sides disagree about a number.

### L5. The default-runtime rule is written three times

Severity: high. Effort: small.

`frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:62-67` exports `defaultRuntimeRef({ desktop })`,
which is the correct home for this decision. Only `parseRuntimeResourceId` calls
it. Three sites reimplement it inline: `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`,
`Settings.tsx:604-606`, and `Settings.tsx:697`.

The related BYOC usability predicate is written four times, and one copy is
wrong. See finding F1.

More broadly, `window.yinshiDesktop` is referenced 27 times across 9 non-test
modules, and `RuntimeRef.location` is inspected 29 times across 9 non-test
modules. Some of those inspections are presentation code that should not care
about transport. `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:321` hides a download link for `byoc`.
`Sidebar.tsx:516` collapses BYOC repositories by default. Both should read a
capability flag on the transport instead.

Suggested fix. Add `runtime/environment.ts` exporting `isDesktop()`. Route all
default-runtime construction through `defaultRuntimeRef`. Add
`runtime/useAvailableRuntimes()` as the single producer of the runtime list,
consumed by both `Sidebar` and `Settings`.

### L6. Smaller duplications

| Item | Locations | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secret-file rule | `workspace_files.py:44-45`, `:113-124`, `:50` (shell regex), `pi_config.py:159-165` | medium |
| Excluded-directory list | `api/sessions.py:21-35` (12 names) vs `workspace_files.py:20-42` (22 names). Already divergent, so the two tree endpoints disagree. | medium |
| Encrypted control-field list | `db.py:842`, `pi_config.py:308`, `:417`, and spelled out at `:377-378` | medium |
| Sidecar newline-JSON framing | `api/terminals.py:72-91` and `services/terminal_journal.py:478-512` | medium |
| Desktop launch config | `main.ts:130-163` (development) vs `runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:165-176` (packaged). Only the packaged path has tests. | medium |

## Part 3: concepts split by operation order

Temporal decomposition organises code around *when* things happen instead of
*what they know*. Three instances were found, and all three are load-bearing.

### D1. The desktop account is split across two modules by timing

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

`accountSession.ts` covers startup and token expiry. `hostedAccessSession.ts`
covers the time between those moments. Neither owns the account. Both manipulate
the same three facts: the active profile, the access token, and the expiry.

This is the direct cause of defect B2.

Suggested fix. Collapse both into one `DesktopAccount` class owning the profile,
the token, the expiry, and one serialising queue. Every path that spends the
stored refresh token then waits on the same promise, so the replay condition is
defined out of existence rather than defended against.

```ts
export class DesktopAccount {
  constructor(options: {
    apiBaseUrl: string;
    fetch: FetchAdapter;
    credentialStore: DesktopCredentialStore;
    now?: () => number;
  });
  get profile(): DesktopCredentialProfile | undefined;
  resume(): Promise<DesktopAccountState>;
  accessToken(): Promise<string>;
  adopt(session: HostedDesktopSession): void;
  clear(): Promise<void>;
}
```

Keep the pure parts where they are. `verifyAccountLease` stays in
`accountLease.ts`. `startHostedSignIn` and `readHostedDesktopTokenResponse` stay
in `hostedAuth.ts`. The offline-lease fallback at `accountSession.ts:50-70` and
`:100-106` becomes private state of `DesktopAccount`, because offline
eligibility is an account question, not a transport question.

Net effect: two modules and two closures become one module and one field.

### D2. `db.py` and `tenant.py` are one module split by database kind

Severity: high. Effort: large.

Covered as finding L2. Named here because the *shape* of the problem is temporal
decomposition, not merely duplication. The split is by which database is being
opened, not by what each module knows. A shared `db/schema.py` and
`db/sqlcipher.py` would restore information hiding.

A related consequence sits at `tenant.py:421-431`. `get_user_db` calls
`_ensure_user_db_schema` inside the connection context manager, so every
database access runs an 87-line DDL script, four `PRAGMA table_info` queries,
and a commit. `api/stream.py` opens eight such blocks per prompt request, at
lines 788, 807, 821, 845, 857, 989, 1027, and 1075. A reader of `get_user_db`
will not guess that reading one row triggers schema DDL. The correct pattern
already exists at `services/prompt_journal.py:113`, which caches initialised
database paths.

### D3. Two supervisors, one process lifecycle

Severity: medium. Effort: small.

| Concern | `sidecarSupervisor.ts` | `helperSupervisor.ts` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Liveness check | 73, 196-198 | 24-26, 124-126 |
| Wait for exit with timeout | 71-86 | 28-42 |
| SIGTERM, wait, SIGKILL, wait, throw | 88-100 | 44-59 |
| Spawn, await readiness, kill on failure | 154-186 | 99-121 |
| Memoised `stop()` | 189-203 | 127-131 |

About 60 lines of parallel logic. The copies have drifted in three ways.
`helperSupervisor.ts:48-49` registers the exit listener before SIGTERM;
`sidecarSupervisor.ts:95-96` sends SIGTERM first. Both are correct today, but a
reader must verify that twice. `SidecarOptions.args` is `readonly string[]` at
`:9` while `StartManagedHelperOptions.arguments` is `string[]` at `:17`, so
`localRuntime.ts:44-52` copies arrays to bridge the difference. The error
messages differ, at `:99` and `:57`.

Suggested fix. Extract `childProcessLifecycle.ts` with a
`startSupervisedChild<Ready>` function parameterised by an `awaitReadiness`
callback, plus `onStarted` and `onStopped` hooks. The sidecar keeps its stale
socket removal, permission assertion, and stdout readiness reader. The helper
keeps its descriptor-3 reader. 343 lines become roughly 230.

## Part 5: parallel subsystems

Four cases where two implementations of one thing coexist. Each doubles the
maintenance cost and creates a class of bug where a fix lands in only one path.

### P1. Two terminal subsystems

`api/terminals.py:273` exposes a direct WebSocket proxy with its own sidecar
framing helpers at `:72-91`. `api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` exposes a polling
channel backed by `services/terminal_journal.py`, with its own framing at
`:478-512`. Both are registered at `main.py:395-396`. Terminal event validation
exists in Python at `terminal_journal.py:404-454` and again in TypeScript at
`terminalChannel.ts:47-59`, with the same 2-to-500 size bounds written in both.

### P2. Two agent-stream subsystems, one of which is unreachable

The SSE path runs through `api/client.ts:514-579` and `api/stream.py`. The polled
journal path runs through `runtime/promptStream.ts` and `api/prompt_runs.py`.
Both share `normalizeEvent` but duplicate transport, status enums, and
cancellation.

The SSE branch appears to be dead. `useAgentStream.ts:127` and `:193` select it
when `runtimeTransport` is falsy. In `pages/Session.tsx:66-70`, `id` and
`transport` both derive from the same `runtimeResource` object, so they are
undefined together, and `sendPrompt` returns early at `useAgentStream.ts:47`.
That makes roughly 90 lines dead and doubles the branching a reader must follow.
Confirm before deleting.

### P3. Two journals with near-identical semantics

`services/prompt_journal.py` (523 lines) and `services/terminal_journal.py` (537
lines) both implement sequenced batch accumulation with the same replay contract.

### P4. `encryptedUpload` bypasses the transport policy layer

`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-341` special-cases uploads.
`runtime/encryptedUpload.ts:150-186` calls `connectEncryptedRunner` directly,
hard-coding `scopes: ["pi.configure"]` at `:159`, skipping `requiredScope`,
`parseByocPath`, and `validateRuntime`. The result is two independent BYOC
request paths under three different session limits.

The guard is also inert. `runtimeTransport.ts:323-338` validates one allowed
upload path, `/api/settings/pi-config/upload`. `encryptedUpload.ts:99-131` never
sends that path; it sends `/uploads`, then `/uploads/{id}/chunks/{i}`, then
`/uploads/{id}/complete`. The validated value is discarded immediately.

so the path stops being a caller concern. Move the session-byte constants into
one `runtime/limits.ts`.

## Part 6: architectural inversions

### A1. A service calls a route and re-parses its own text output

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

`services/prompt_journal.py:64` calls `yinshi.api.stream.prompt_session`, which
is a FastAPI route function. Lines 65-87 then parse the SSE text that route
produced back into dictionaries: split on the blank-line separator, strip the
`data:` prefix, call `json.loads`.

So `services` calls `api`, which calls `services`. A text wire format is
serialised and immediately deserialised inside one process. Every public method
on the journal takes a `Request` parameter, at `:105`, `:191`, and `:245`, so the
module cannot be used outside an HTTP request.

Any change to SSE framing in `api/stream.py` silently breaks the durable journal.
The docstring at `:63` acknowledges the coupling: "Adapt the existing SSE route
generator".

The module graph also contains a cycle. `api/deps.py:9` imports from `db.py`,
while `services/prompt_journal.py:17` imports from `api/deps.py`.

Suggested fix. Extract the shared prompt-execution generator into
`services/prompt_turn.py`, returning an async iterator of event dictionaries.
`api/stream.py` wraps it in SSE framing. The journal consumes it directly. This
removes the cycle and the text round trip together.

### A2. The backend imports itself across a network boundary

Severity: medium. Documented, not necessarily a defect.

The BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI application in-process.
`runner_worker.py:264-293` calls `main.create_app(mode="worker", ...)` through a
deferred import, and `worker_runtime.py:29-40` dispatches into it over ASGI with
no listening socket. One codebase acts as both control plane and remote worker,
separated only by `app.state.mode`.

This is a deliberate and reasonable choice: it guarantees that the worker
implements exactly the same routes. It is recorded here because the deferred
import at `runner_worker.py:264` is the only thing preventing a circular import,
and because it is not obvious to a new reader.

### A3. Two runtime vocabularies that do not line up

Severity: medium. Effort: small.

The frontend `RuntimeRef.location` union is `local | hosted | byoc`, at
`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`. The backend `AppMode` is
`desktop | hosted | worker`, at `main.py:415-457`. Frontend `local` maps to
backend `desktop`. Frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker`. Deployment material
uses a third vocabulary: runner, sidecar, helper.

Nothing in the code states or enforces the mapping, and no file records it.

Backend mode branching occurs in twelve places, including a distinct middleware
stack at `main.py:309-322`, a fixed `desktop-local` tenant at `:344-352`, a
different content security policy at `:361-363`, and a router split at
`:379-412`.

Suggested fix. Choose one vocabulary. Failing that, record the mapping in one
file and reference it from both sides.

### A4. Five unrelated modules named for "runtime"

Severity: medium. Effort: small.

| Module | Lines | Actual concern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `desktop_runtime.py` | 164 | Electron helper process: socket bind, readiness pipe, Uvicorn boot |
| `worker_runtime.py` | 168 | In-process ASGI dispatcher with validation |
| `services/sidecar_runtime.py` | 663 | Container mounts, home layout, pi session paths |
| `services/git_runtime.py` | 69 | One ephemeral GitHub App credential payload |
| `services/workspace_runtime_paths.py` | 78 | Workspace and repo host-path validation |

There is no shared code and no duplicated logic here. The problem is the
opposite: "runtime" is a vague name applied to five different things, so a reader
must open each file to learn what it does. The same word also names the frontend
`runtime/` directory and the desktop `runtimeSecrets.ts`, neither of which is
related to any of the above.

On the desktop side, `runtimeSecrets.ts` is worth renaming to `helperKeyStore.ts`.
`RuntimeSecretStore` at `:48-89` has no link to the user account; it generates
three local encryption keys for the Python helper. Its current name places it
beside `credentialStore` and `accountSession` in a reader's mind.

rather than duplicating primitives.

`crypto/noiseIk.ts` hides all Noise state machine detail behind a six-member
interface at `:36-43`. Key material is zeroed on every path, at `:151`, `:344`,
`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:397`, and `encryptedUpload.ts:139-140`.

`desktop/src/secureJsonStore.ts:100-170` writes to a temporary file, syncs both
file and directory, asserts permissions before and after, and reads with
`O_NOFOLLOW`. Three methods.

`desktop/src/accountLease.ts:84-159` is pure, total, and self-contained. Every
failure path funnels through one `invalidLease()` helper, keeping the error path
short.

`desktop/src/credentialStore.ts:160-262` serialises vault mutations through one
`#enqueue` field. Version-1 records migrate to version 2 during validation at
`:97-105`, which is the right home for the migration.

`services/desktop_auth.py:125-402` is genuinely deep.
`exchange_desktop_authorization_code` takes three parameters and hides PKCE
verification, single-use code consumption, device creation, and token issuance.

`services/workspace_runtime_paths.py:57-78` is a correct deep abstraction: one
call repairs the checkout, validates both paths against tenant storage, and
installs guardrails. Three of four callers use it.

`runtime/runtimeRef.ts:29-54` round-trips base64url and rejects non-canonical
encodings by re-encoding and comparing at `:50`.

`config.py:287-348` fails closed at startup on dangerous combinations, such as
no-auth mode bound to a non-loopback host.

`main.py:63-105` handles both the declared content length and the streamed case
in its body-limit middleware, which is commonly missed.

Dependency injection is applied consistently and without ceremony across the
frontend and desktop. See `RuntimeTransportDependencies`,
`RunnerClientDependencies`, `RuntimeResolverDependencies`, and the
`DesktopAppController` contract.

Comments generally explain reasoning rather than restating code.
`sidecar_runtime.py:437-441` explains why the repo is mounted at its host path so
git worktree pointers resolve. `sidecar.js:681-684` and `:1751-1756` record
reasoning that the code cannot express. Preserve these through any decomposition.

The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component. It knows nothing about
runtimes, tenants, or Noise. It is a clean extraction boundary.

---

## Suggested order of work

Sequenced so that early items are cheap, close real defects, or remove code that
later items would otherwise have to move.

**Stage 1: close live defects.** B1 session eviction, then B2 through the
`DesktopAccount` merge (D1). Both are small and both fix user-visible failures.

**Stage 2: pure deletion.** L3 storage profile table (about 130 lines). S1 and S2
container wrappers (about 87 lines plus 7 call sites). S15 through S17 dead code.
P2 dead SSE path, after confirming it is unreachable (about 90 lines). This stage
removes roughly 400 lines and touches no behaviour.

**Stage 3: single-home the small decisions.** F1 runner usability predicate,
which closes a real inconsistency. L5 default-runtime rule. L6 remaining
duplications: secret rules, excluded directories, encrypted field list, launch
config, profile layout, secret validation.

**Stage 4: fix the inversions.** A1 prompt journal, extracting
`services/prompt_turn.py`. This also starts F2.

**Stage 5: restore layering.** L2 and D2 database schema and SQLCipher
consolidation. F2 remaining `api/stream.py` extraction, with
`services/session_store.py` and `services/repo_store.py`. F6 frontend boundary
mappers and named resource functions.

**Stage 6: decompose the large files.** F3 sidecar, in the five-step order given.
F4 `main.ts`. F5 frontend god components, after stages 3 and 5 have removed the
logic they currently inline.

**Stage 7: unify the generated surfaces.** L1 route table generation. L4 protocol
constant generation. L7 API type generation. Highest coordination cost, and best
attempted once the earlier stages have reduced the number of hand-written call
sites.

Renaming work from A3 and A4 can be folded into whichever stage touches the
affected files.

---

## Open questions

These were found while tracing and need a decision from someone with product
context.

1. Is the RPC envelope `v: 2` at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483` intentional
   against `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `runner_rpc.py:17`?
2. Does the backend accept the `query` key that the frontend always sends? It is
   absent from `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`.
3. Is `api/terminals.py` still live, or superseded by `api/terminal_channels.py`?
   Both are registered at `main.py:395-396`.
4. Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` still live, or superseded by `promptStream.ts`?
   The analysis in P2 suggests it is unreachable.
5. Are the three session byte caps (64 KiB, 256 KiB, 128 MiB) intentional per
   channel, or drift?

arguments.content:
# Software Design Review

Date: 2026-08-07
Scope: entire codebase, four components, roughly 40,000 source lines.
Lens: "A Philosophy of Software Design" red-flag checklist.
Status: findings only. Nothing was implemented.

| Component | Path | Non-test lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backend | `backend/src/yinshi/` | 23,124 |
| Frontend | `frontend/src/` | 11,053 |
| Desktop | `desktop/src/` | 3,168 |
| Sidecar | `sidecar/src/` | 2,584 |

Excluded: `backend/.venv`, `node_modules`, `frontend/dist`, `desktop/dist`, `desktop/release`.

---

## Executive summary

The codebase has strong low-level design. Cryptographic primitives, the Noise
handshake, the secure JSON store, and the account lease verifier are deep
modules with simple interfaces. Test coverage is broad, at 55 backend test files
and 20 frontend test files.

The weakness is at the boundaries. The same design decision is written in
several places, and in several cases the copies have already drifted apart.
Three problems recur across every component.

1. One decision has many homes. The API route surface is enumerated four times,
   in three languages. The database schema is written twice. The runner storage
   profile table is written twice. The default-runtime rule is written three
   times.
2. Concepts are split by operation order rather than by information hiding. The
   desktop account is split across two modules by the moment each is used. The
   backend database layer is split by which database it opens.
3. Transport-layer files hold business logic. `api/stream.py` has 770 lines
   before its first route. `Sidebar.tsx` holds six unrelated responsibilities.
   `sidecar.js` holds thirteen.

Two findings are live defects rather than design debt. Both are small to fix.
They are B1, where the session map never evicts, and B2, where a concurrent
token refresh can revoke the user device.

---

## Part 1: live defects

### B1. The sidecar session map has no removal path

Severity: high. Effort: small.

`sidecar/src/sidecar.js:934` creates `activeSessions`. It is written at `:1655`
and `:1739`, and read at `:1624`, `:1683`, and `:1966`. The only removal is
`clear()` at `:2005`, inside `cleanup()`, which runs at process exit.

There is no delete, no time-to-live, and no size cap. The protocol has no
dispose message, and `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py` never sends one.
Socket close detaches terminals at `:1129-1132` and leaves sessions untouched.

Each retained entry holds a live pi session with model context, a settings
manager, and an open session file handle. See `SessionManager.open` at `:205`.
In the desktop app the sidecar runs for the whole application lifetime, so every
session a user opens stays resident until quit.

The inconsistency inside the same file is instructive. OAuth flows have a
30-minute time-to-live and a cap of 8, at `:35` and `:1368`. Terminals are
removed on exit at `:1017-1020`. Pi sessions alone have neither policy.

Suggested fix. Move the map into `pi/sessionRegistry.js` with a maximum entry
count and an idle time-to-live. On eviction, call `unsubscribe()` and
`piSession.dispose()`. Add a `session_release` message so the backend can
release deterministically.

### B2. Two refresh paths race, and the loser revokes the device

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

The backend treats a replayed refresh token as a compromise signal. At
`backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_auth.py:244-255`, presenting an
already-rotated token revokes the whole device and calls
`signal_desktop_device_revoked`.

The desktop app has two independent paths that spend the stored refresh token,
and only one of them is serialised.

- `HostedAccessSession.getAccessToken` at
  `desktop/src/hostedAccessSession.ts:57-84` de-duplicates concurrent refreshes
  through a `#refresh` promise and guards stale writes through `#epoch`. This
  path is correct.
- `DesktopAppController.switchProfile` at `desktop/src/appController.ts:110-121`
  calls `resumeAccount`, wired at `desktop/src/main.ts:301-309` to call
  `resumeDesktopAccount` directly. This path never touches `#refresh`.

Both eventually reach `desktop/src/accountSession.ts:88-99`, which posts the
stored refresh token.

The two are wired 25 lines apart in the same function.
`desktop/src/main.ts:285-292` builds `HostedAccessSession` with a callback into
`resumeDesktopAccount`. Then `main.ts:301-309` builds a second closure calling
the same function and pushing the result back in. The same operation appears
twice, in two directions.

A renderer request that triggers a refresh through `hostedApiGateway` can
overlap a profile switch. The second refresh presents a token the first has
already rotated. The backend then revokes the device, and the user is signed out
with no explanation.

Suggested fix is in Part 3, finding D1.

---

## Part 2: one decision, many homes

This is the dominant structural problem. Each item below is information leakage
in the strict sense. A single design decision that a reader must find in several
files, kept consistent only by hand.

### L1. The API route surface is enumerated four times, in three languages

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

| Location | Purpose | Patterns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/src/yinshi/api/*.py` | the actual FastAPI routers | 81 routes |
| `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` | server-side scope enforcement | 21 |
| `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` | client-side scope selection | 18 |
| `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:12-192` | Electron bridge allowlist | 20 |

Adding one route now requires four coordinated edits across three languages.
Nothing enforces the correspondence, and no test asserts that the tables agree.

The copies have already drifted. The backend handles four pi-upload path
patterns at `runner_rpc.py:206-215`. The frontend table has no upload entries at
all, so `runtimeTransport.ts` would reject them. The upload flow works only
because it bypasses the transport layer entirely. See finding P4.

Each table has a defensible reason to exist. The backend table is authoritative
enforcement. The desktop table limits what a compromised renderer can reach.
Deleting either one is therefore the wrong fix.

Suggested fix. Declare the route-to-scope mapping once, as FastAPI dependency
metadata attached to each route. Build the backend table at startup by walking
the registered routes, so an unregistered route fails loudly instead of becoming
silently unreachable. Generate the frontend and desktop tables at build time from
the OpenAPI document. Divergence then becomes a build failure rather than a
runtime rejection.

### L2. The database schema is written twice, and the migrations have drifted

Severity: high. Effort: large.

`backend/src/yinshi/db.py:33-120` holds `SCHEMA_SQL`. `tenant.py:66-152` holds
`USER_SCHEMA_SQL`. A direct diff of the two regions reports exactly one
difference. `tenant.py` omits the `owner_email` column.

Eighty-seven of eighty-eight lines are duplicated verbatim. That covers six
create-table statements, six indexes, and three triggers. Every column addition
must be made twice.

The migration logic is duplicated too, and it has already produced inconsistent
state. `db.py:342-384` applies five numbered migrations behind a `schema_version`
table. `tenant.py:153-175` applies four of the same column additions with no
version tracking, re-running `PRAGMA table_info` on every call. Both migrations
add `pi_context_version` with a default of zero, at `db.py:379` and
`tenant.py:172-174`. Both base schemas declare a default of one, at `db.py:66`
and `tenant.py:97`. New databases and migrated databases therefore start in
different states.

That inconsistency is real rather than hypothetical. `api/stream.py:571-595`
exists to detect and repair it at request time.

Six SQLCipher helpers are near-duplicates as well.

| Concern | `db.py` | `tenant.py` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Driver module names | 25 | 29-32 |
| Driver loading | 130-140 | 183-204 |
| Keyed connection open | 164-191 | 216-247 |
| Plaintext readability probe | 193-206 | 257-270 |
| Encrypted integrity validation | 208-228 | 299-313 |
| Plaintext to encrypted migration | 230-293 | 315-343 |

The two probes at `tenant.py:257-270` and `db.py:193-206` differ only by one
file-existence call.

Suggested fix. Create `db/schema.py` with one parameterised schema builder and
one ordered migration list keyed by version, applied to both database kinds.
Create `db/sqlcipher.py` holding the driver loader, keyed open, plaintext probe,
integrity validator, and migration, parameterised by a key-derivation callable.
The two current modules then hold only policy and connection scoping. Expect
well under the current combined 1,305 lines.

### L3. The runner storage profile table is duplicated verbatim

Severity: high. Effort: small.

`runner_agent.py:57-121` and `services/runners.py:58-120` hold the same
`RunnerStorageProfileSpec` dataclass with 11 fields, and the same 63-line
`_STORAGE_PROFILES` dictionary with three entries. A direct diff reports only a
one-line docstring difference and a blank line. Every profile value is identical.

The eight supporting constants are duplicated at `runner_agent.py:48-55` and
`services/runners.py:40-47`. So is the storage-profile literal type, at
`runner_agent.py:33-37` and `services/runners.py:24-28`. So is
`_storage_profile_spec`, at `runner_agent.py:182` and `services/runners.py:157`.

The control plane validates reported runner capabilities against this table at
`services/runners.py:313`. The agent uses the same table to choose its own
defaults at `runner_agent.py:212-216`. Editing one copy alone makes runners fail
validation against the control plane, with no local signal.

Suggested fix. Move the literal type, constants, dataclass, dictionary, and
lookup helper into `runner_storage_profiles.py`. Import from both sides. This
deletes about 130 duplicated lines and is the cheapest high-value change in the
report.

### L4. The Noise wire protocol is re-derived independently per language

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

There is no shared schema, interface definition, or generated artifact. Matching
literal constants are written twice, in two different crypto stacks. Python uses
`noiseprotocol` at `services/runner_noise.py:11-20`. The browser uses
`@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` at `crypto/noiseIk.ts:1-6`. Parity is maintained
only by hand.

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name | `runner_noise.py:22` | `noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `runner_noise.py:26` | `noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `runner_noise.py:24` | `noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `runner_noise.py:25` | `noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `runner_noise_session.py:24` | `noiseIk.ts:14` |
| Prologue tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `runner_noise_session.py:23` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9` |

A protocol change requires coordinated edits in seventeen files across backend
and frontend, plus their test mirrors.

Two open discrepancies surfaced while tracing this. The frontend request
envelope sends `v: 2` at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483`, while the backend
accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `runner_rpc.py:17` and does not
list the `query` key the frontend always sends. Both deserve confirmation.
Separately, the session byte cap has three values. It is 64 KiB at
`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:15`, 256 KiB at `runtimeTransport.ts:90`, and 128 MiB
at `encryptedUpload.ts:10`.

Suggested fix. Declare the constants and envelope schema in one machine-readable
file. Generate the Python and TypeScript constant modules from it. This will not
unify the two crypto implementations, and it should not try to. It removes the
class of failure where the two sides disagree about a number.

### L5. The default-runtime rule is written three times

Severity: high. Effort: small.

`frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:62-67` exports `defaultRuntimeRef({ desktop })`,
which is the correct home for this decision. Only `parseRuntimeResourceId` calls
it. Three sites reimplement it inline, at `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`,
`Settings.tsx:604-606`, and `Settings.tsx:697`.

The related BYOC usability predicate is written four times, and one copy is
wrong. See finding F1.

More broadly, `window.yinshiDesktop` is referenced 27 times across 9 non-test
modules, and `RuntimeRef.location` is inspected 29 times across 9 non-test
modules. Some of those inspections are presentation code that should not care
about transport. `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:321` hides a download link for `byoc`.
`Sidebar.tsx:516` collapses BYOC repositories by default. Both should read a
capability flag on the transport instead.

Suggested fix. Add `runtime/environment.ts` exporting `isDesktop()`. Route all
default-runtime construction through `defaultRuntimeRef`. Add
`runtime/useAvailableRuntimes()` as the single producer of the runtime list,
consumed by both `Sidebar` and `Settings`.

### L6. Smaller duplications

| Item | Locations | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secret-file rule | `workspace_files.py:44-45`, `:113-124`, `:50` (shell regex), `pi_config.py:159-165` | medium |
| Excluded-directory list | `api/sessions.py:21-35` lists 12 names against 22 in `workspace_files.py:20-42`. Already divergent, so the two tree endpoints disagree. | medium |
| Encrypted control-field list | `db.py:842`, `pi_config.py:308`, `:417`, and spelled out at `:377-378` | medium |
| Sidecar newline-JSON framing | `api/terminals.py:72-91` and `services/terminal_journal.py:478-512` | medium |
| Desktop launch config | `main.ts:130-163` for development against `runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:165-176` for packaged. Only the packaged path has tests. | medium |
| Profile directory layout | `main.ts:93-105`, `runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:104-152`, `main.ts:524-527` | medium |
| Runtime-secret validation | `runtimeSecrets.ts:20-46` and `runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:72-82`, identical regexes | medium |
| Relay frame byte cap | `runner_relay.py:17` and `runner_agent_relay.py:16` | low |
| `DesktopProfileSummary` type | `credentialStore.ts:22-26` and `desktopApi.ts:29-33` | low |
| `RESOURCE_ID_PATTERN` | 5 frontend modules | low |
| base64url encoding | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:85-96`, `runtimeRef.ts:17-27`, `encryptedUpload.ts:22-26` | low |
| `formatTimestamp` | `Settings.tsx:22-27`, `CloudRunnerSection.tsx:113-118`, `PiConfigSection.tsx:22-27`, identical bodies | low |

### L7. No generated API types

Severity: medium. Effort: medium.

There is no OpenAPI code generation. `frontend/package.json` has no generate
script, and the backend serves `/openapi.json` only when `debug` is true, at
`main.py:451`. Twenty-two request and response shapes are hand-written twice,
in `backend/src/yinshi/models.py` and `frontend/src/api/client.ts`. Terminal
channel shapes, prompt run shapes, and the run status enum are duplicated
outside those two files as well.

This ranks below L1 through L5 because the failure mode is a type error at the
boundary rather than silent divergence. It is listed because it is the root
cause of finding F6.

---

## Part 3: concepts split by operation order

Temporal decomposition organises code around the order in which things happen,
rather than around what each module knows. Three instances were found, and all
three are load-bearing.

### D1. The desktop account is split across two modules by timing

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

`accountSession.ts` covers startup and token expiry. `hostedAccessSession.ts`
covers the time between those moments. Neither owns the account. Both manipulate
the same three facts: the active profile, the access token, and the expiry.

This is the direct cause of defect B2.

Suggested fix. Collapse both into one `DesktopAccount` class owning the profile,
the token, the expiry, and one serialising queue. Every path that spends the
stored refresh token then waits on the same promise, so the replay condition is
defined out of existence rather than defended against.

```ts
export class DesktopAccount {
  constructor(options: {
    apiBaseUrl: string;
    fetch: FetchAdapter;
    credentialStore: DesktopCredentialStore;
    now?: () => number;
  });
  get profile(): DesktopCredentialProfile | undefined;
  resume(): Promise<DesktopAccountState>;
  accessToken(): Promise<string>;
  adopt(session: HostedDesktopSession): void;
  clear(): Promise<void>;
}
```

Keep the pure parts where they are. `verifyAccountLease` stays in
`accountLease.ts`. `startHostedSignIn` and `readHostedDesktopTokenResponse` stay
in `hostedAuth.ts`. The offline-lease fallback at `accountSession.ts:50-70` and
`:100-106` becomes private state of `DesktopAccount`, because offline
eligibility is an account question rather than a transport question.

Net effect: two modules and two closures become one module and one field.

### D2. `db.py` and `tenant.py` are one module split by database kind

Severity: high. Effort: large.

Covered as finding L2. It is named again here because the shape of the problem
is temporal decomposition and not merely duplication. The split follows which
database is being opened, and it ignores what each module knows. A shared
`db/schema.py` and `db/sqlcipher.py` would restore information hiding.

A related consequence sits at `tenant.py:421-431`. `get_user_db` calls
`_ensure_user_db_schema` inside the connection context manager, so every
database access runs an 87-line DDL script, four `PRAGMA table_info` queries,
and a commit. `api/stream.py` opens eight such blocks per prompt request, at

## Part 5: parallel subsystems

Four cases where two implementations of one thing coexist. Each doubles the
maintenance cost and creates a class of bug where a fix lands in only one path.

### P1. Two terminal subsystems

`api/terminals.py:273` exposes a direct WebSocket proxy with its own sidecar
framing helpers at `:72-91`. `api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` exposes a polling
channel backed by `services/terminal_journal.py`, with its own framing at
`:478-512`. Both are registered at `main.py:395-396`. Terminal event validation
exists in Python at `terminal_journal.py:404-454` and again in TypeScript at
`terminalChannel.ts:47-59`, with the same 2-to-500 size bounds written in both.

### P2. Two agent-stream subsystems, one of which is unreachable

The SSE path runs through `api/client.ts:514-579` and `api/stream.py`. The polled
journal path runs through `runtime/promptStream.ts` and `api/prompt_runs.py`.
Both share `normalizeEvent` and duplicate transport, status enums, and
cancellation.

The SSE branch appears to be dead. `useAgentStream.ts:127` and `:193` select it
when `runtimeTransport` is falsy. In `pages/Session.tsx:66-70`, `id` and
`transport` both derive from the same `runtimeResource` object, so they are
undefined together, and `sendPrompt` returns early at `useAgentStream.ts:47`.
That makes roughly 90 lines dead and doubles the branching a reader must follow.
Confirm before deleting.

### P3. Two journals with near-identical semantics

`services/prompt_journal.py` at 523 lines and `services/terminal_journal.py` at
537 lines both implement sequenced batch accumulation with the same replay
contract.

### P4. `encryptedUpload` bypasses the transport policy layer

`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-341` special-cases uploads.
`runtime/encryptedUpload.ts:150-186` calls `connectEncryptedRunner` directly,
hard-coding `scopes: ["pi.configure"]` at `:159`, skipping `requiredScope`,
`parseByocPath`, and `validateRuntime`. The result is two independent BYOC
request paths under three different session limits.

The guard is also inert. `runtimeTransport.ts:323-338` validates one allowed
upload path, `/api/settings/pi-config/upload`. `encryptedUpload.ts:99-131` never
sends that path. It sends `/uploads`, then `/uploads/{id}/chunks/{i}`, then
`/uploads/{id}/complete`. The validated value is discarded immediately.

Suggested fix. Give `RuntimeTransport` an explicit `uploadPiConfig(file)` method
so the path stops being a caller concern. Move the session-byte constants into
one `runtime/limits.ts`.

## Part 6: architectural inversions

### A1. A service calls a route and re-parses its own text output

Severity: high. Effort: medium.

`services/prompt_journal.py:64` calls `yinshi.api.stream.prompt_session`, which
is a FastAPI route function. Lines 65-87 then parse the SSE text that route
produced back into dictionaries. They split on the blank-line separator, strip
the `data:` prefix, and call `json.loads`.

So `services` calls `api`, which calls `services`. A text wire format is
serialised and immediately deserialised inside one process. Every public method
on the journal takes a `Request` parameter, at `:105`, `:191`, and `:245`, so the
module cannot be used outside an HTTP request.

Any change to SSE framing in `api/stream.py` silently breaks the durable journal.
The docstring at `:63` acknowledges the coupling, reading "Adapt the existing SSE
route generator".

The module graph also contains a cycle. `api/deps.py:9` imports from `db.py`,
while `services/prompt_journal.py:17` imports from `api/deps.py`.

Suggested fix. Extract the shared prompt-execution generator into
`services/prompt_turn.py`, returning an async iterator of event dictionaries.
`api/stream.py` wraps it in SSE framing. The journal consumes it directly. This
removes the cycle and the text round trip together.

### A2. The backend imports itself across a network boundary

Severity: medium. Recorded for clarity rather than as a defect.

The BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI application in-process.
`runner_worker.py:264-293` calls `main.create_app(mode="worker", ...)` through a
deferred import, and `worker_runtime.py:29-40` dispatches into it over ASGI with
no listening socket. One codebase acts as both control plane and remote worker,
separated only by `app.state.mode`.

This is a deliberate and reasonable choice, because it guarantees that the
worker implements exactly the same routes. It appears here because the deferred
import at `runner_worker.py:264` is the only thing preventing a circular import,
and because a new reader will not expect it.

### A3. Two runtime vocabularies that do not line up

Severity: medium. Effort: small.

The frontend `RuntimeRef.location` union is `local | hosted | byoc`, at
`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`. The backend `AppMode` is
`desktop | hosted | worker`, at `main.py:415-457`. Frontend `local` maps to
backend `desktop`. Frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker`. Deployment material
uses a third vocabulary of runner, sidecar, and helper.

Nothing in the code states or enforces the mapping, and no file records it.

Backend mode branching occurs in twelve places, including a distinct middleware
stack at `main.py:309-322`, a fixed `desktop-local` tenant at `:344-352`, a
different content security policy at `:361-363`, and a router split at
`:379-412`.

Suggested fix. Choose one vocabulary. Failing that, record the mapping in one
file and reference it from both sides.

### A4. Five unrelated modules named for "runtime"

Severity: medium. Effort: small.

| Module | Lines | Actual concern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `desktop_runtime.py` | 164 | Electron helper process: socket bind, readiness pipe, Uvicorn boot |
| `worker_runtime.py` | 168 | In-process ASGI dispatcher with validation |
| `services/sidecar_runtime.py` | 663 | Container mounts, home layout, pi session paths |
| `services/git_runtime.py` | 69 | One ephemeral GitHub App credential payload |
| `services/workspace_runtime_paths.py` | 78 | Workspace and repo host-path validation |

There is no shared code and no duplicated logic here. The problem is the
opposite. The word "runtime" is a vague name applied to five different things,
so a reader must open each file to learn what it does. The same word also names
the frontend `runtime/` directory and the desktop `runtimeSecrets.ts`, neither
of which relates to any of the above.

On the desktop side, `runtimeSecrets.ts` is worth renaming to `helperKeyStore.ts`.
`RuntimeSecretStore` at `:48-89` has no link to the user account. It generates
three local encryption keys for the Python helper. Its current name places it
beside `credentialStore` and `accountSession` in a reader's mind.

## What is already good

These should survive any restructuring.

`services/crypto.py:47-243` holds one HKDF derivation and two envelope formats.
The interface is much simpler than the implementation.
`services/control_encryption.py` correctly stays a thin policy layer over it
instead of duplicating primitives.

`crypto/noiseIk.ts` hides all Noise state machine detail behind a six-member
interface at `:36-43`. Key material is zeroed on every path, at `:151`, `:344`,
`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:397`, and `encryptedUpload.ts:139-140`.

`desktop/src/secureJsonStore.ts:100-170` writes to a temporary file, syncs both
file and directory, asserts permissions before and after, and reads with
`O_NOFOLLOW`. Three methods.

`desktop/src/accountLease.ts:84-159` is pure, total, and self-contained. Every
failure path funnels through one `invalidLease()` helper, keeping the error path
short.

`desktop/src/credentialStore.ts:160-262` serialises vault mutations through one
`#enqueue` field. Version-1 records migrate to version 2 during validation at
`:97-105`, which is the right home for the migration.

`services/desktop_auth.py:125-402` is genuinely deep.
`exchange_desktop_authorization_code` takes three parameters and hides PKCE
verification, single-use code consumption, device creation, and token issuance.

`services/workspace_runtime_paths.py:57-78` is a correct deep abstraction. One
call repairs the checkout, validates both paths against tenant storage, and
installs guardrails. Three of four callers use it.

`runtime/runtimeRef.ts:29-54` round-trips base64url and rejects non-canonical
encodings by re-encoding and comparing at `:50`.

`config.py:287-348` fails closed at startup on dangerous combinations, such as
no-auth mode bound to a non-loopback host.

`main.py:63-105` handles both the declared content length and the streamed case
in its body-limit middleware, which is commonly missed.

Dependency injection is applied consistently and without ceremony across the
frontend and desktop. See `RuntimeTransportDependencies`,
`RunnerClientDependencies`, `RuntimeResolverDependencies`, and the
`DesktopAppController` contract.

Comments generally explain reasoning instead of restating code.
`sidecar_runtime.py:437-441` explains why the repo is mounted at its host path so
git worktree pointers resolve. `sidecar.js:681-684` and `:1751-1756` record
reasoning that the code cannot express. Preserve these through any decomposition.

The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component. It knows nothing about
runtimes, tenants, or Noise, and it forms a clean extraction boundary.
